power closure is BOUNDED, not demonstrated: at the coarse rung interior add_flux_monitor planes and the port route agree to within the column-power tolerance, but both sit at the float32 field-noise floor of that rung, so the witness caps the disagreement rather than resolving it. The witness is independent in the PLANE INDEX ONLY - both routes integrate the same transverse window with the same uniform dA through the same flux kernel, so an area-weighting or shared-kernel error cancels in both ratios, and neither route sees the reference-plane de-embedding, which is phase-only. That measurement landed on main in PR #870

accuracy statement for the normalize=False lane (issue #873, closed as a stated accuracy, not a defect): on an EMPTY WR-90 guide its column-power error falls with mesh refinement (fixture_v18_close.json, the gated artifact). The flux lane's empty-guide reading is a construction (its reference run is the device run), so the comparisons that carry weight are the dielectric slab in the same artifact and the interior monitors. Mechanism named in docs/design_notes/waveguide_driven_plane_near_field_composition_results.md, measured on the same artifact: the templates are cell-centred while Ez and Hy are node-registered in the broad-wall direction; the half-cell offset launches a TE20 near field at the driven port and reads it back as TE10, second order in dx; TE20's decay matches the attenuation constant tabulated before the run; the note's pre-declared rule came out NOT CONFIRMED because it named TE30. For a result you can cite, use the single-family extractors separately -- compute_msl_s_matrix(...) for the microstrip line, compute_coaxial_two_port(...) / compute_coaxial_line_reflection(...) for the coax. The power-wave cross-family normalization (per-port sqrt(Z0) division before the two-drive solve) is validated by planted-voltage unit tests under UNEQUAL port impedances, independent of any FDTD run. The corrected settled run (PR #837) is NOT passive: the MSL-driven column reads excess power, and the shared passivity guard raises on the result -- compute_coax_msl_transition(...) refuses that matrix by default (strict_passivity=True, raising ValueError), and strict_passivity=False returns it with a UserWarning instead. The over-read sits in the MSL side's power-wave normalization and is measured by the S-matrix's own column power and a Poynting flux box on the same run. The mechanism is unresolved and will not be attributed on this lane (issue #838). Fitted Im(gamma) against analytic beta says the matrix pencil is locking onto the right mode. That PHASE-CONSTANT witness clears neither the wave-amplitude split nor the power normalization: the echo ratio verdict is FLOOR on the MSL side and RESOLVED on the coax side; the passivity eigenvalue verdict is EXTRACTOR. Do not cite this family as a validated transition.

On the same record the echo-ratio verdict is FLOOR on the MSL side (the non-driven MSL port's signal is extractor floor) and RESOLVED on the coax side; the passivity eigenvalue lambda_min(I - S^H S) verdict is EXTRACTOR

the V/I-vs-Poynting-flux oracle bounds the single-family MSL lane's power scale against the true Poynting flux and excludes the transition's over-read: scripts/diagnostics/msl_vi_flux_oracle/msl_vi_flux_oracle.json checks aligned and mixed-cell meshes, both HELD. Its retired ratio_proxy_span replay is a mutation control showing the oracle can distinguish the corrected span. The thru-coupon golden's column power cannot settle this on its own: a per-port amplitude constant cancels from S between like ports. The oracle is structurally blind to the power-preserving rescale (V, I) -> (aV, I/a): R = Re(V*conj(I))/flux is exactly invariant, so a defect moving V and I in that opposing pattern would pass both the ratio and its admissibility witnesses while corrupting every S value downstream (scripts/diagnostics/msl_vi_flux_oracle.py)

the single-family MSL lane is not defect-free either: its equal-reference notch-filter output records a small coherent power excess (PR #987), though it does not carry the transition's power over-read

the lanes share helpers: compute_msl_mode_profile, setup_msl_port and make_msl_port_sources (rfx/sparams/coax.py, rfx/runners/uniform.py and rfx/runners/nonuniform.py), the analytic reference hammerstad_jensen_z0_eps_eff (rfx/sparams/coax.py, rfx/sparams/msl.py), and the voltage line-integral helper msl_modal_voltage. The difference is downstream: the transition forms its wave amplitudes from V alone (a matrix-pencil fit on the modal voltage ladder), the single-family lane from V and I

the corrected settled run's record is tracked under scripts/diagnostics/_coax_msl_transition_settled_run_logs/ (PR #837); the run log's vessl_run_id field is an unfilled placeholder and the result JSON has no such key; the code state is pinned in the result JSON

the shared passivity guard is ONE-SIDED: it flags only a column power ABOVE its limit, never a column power far BELOW the incident power on a nominally lossless structure. Disclosure only; the guard is unchanged here
raw cond_a is dominated by per-drive amplitude scale, not geometric near-degeneracy -- read cond_a_equilibrated on CoaxMSLTransitionResult instead

the MSL side is extracted via the coax matrix-pencil fit (coaxial_line_reflection_from_plane_voltages) rather than the mixed lane's own N-probe fit, a deliberate deviation made because the coax fit deterministically pins the propagation-constant branch while the N-probe fit's sign is documented as unstable

the registered impedance= on add_coaxial_port(...)/add_msl_port(...) sizes only the feed resistor / termination and (for coax) the TEM source amplitude calibration; the power-wave normalization (z0_ref) always uses the analytic TEM / Hammerstad-Jensen Z0 the method computes itself, so the registered impedance= is NOT the reference impedance of the returned s_params -- the method emits a divergence advisory when either port's registered impedance diverges from the analytic Z0 it actually uses (issue #581 review N2)
